evidence.excerpt: Digital twin frameworks — virtual replicas of physical supply chains updated by real-time sensor data — offer a new paradigm for proactive spoilage management in perishable food logistics. This paper describes the integration of validated predictive microbial growth models for Botrytis cinerea and total aerobic bacteria into a digital twin architecture developed for Serbian berry cold-chain operations. The system ingests temperature and relative humidity streams from IoT sensors placed within refrigerated transport units and storage rooms, feeding real-time inputs into a model library calibrated for raspberry, blueberry, and strawberry substrates. A graphical dashboard presents logistics managers with dynamically updated remaining shelf-life estimates and spoilage risk scores for each consignment. A 12-month pilot deployment covering four exporting companies and 240 consignments demonstrated that digital twin alerts correctly flagged 88% of consignments subsequently confirmed to exhibit elevated spoilage at destination. False-positive rates were 9%, attributed primarily to anomalous sensor placement near evaporator coils. Integration with enterprise resource planning (ERP) systems for automated re-routing decisions is discussed as a near-term development pathway. The study establishes a reproducible blueprint for deploying predictive microbiology within commercial cold-chain digital twin platforms in the Serbian fruit export sector.
